items.summary:
While many of the headlines leading up to the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony this weekend were about who wouldn’t be there, our highlights from Saturday night’s (Nov. 14) show at L.A.’s Peacock Theatre are all about who showed up and showed out.

The night was bookended by two surprise performances, starting with 2005 inductees U2 playing a brand-new song and a classic to kick things off and ending with 2001 inductees Aerosmith joining forces with 2009 inductees Run-DMC to perform their pioneering rock/hip-hop mash-up “Walk This Way,” a top five Billboard Hot 100 smash in 1986.

Related 

Phil Collins Tells Rock Hall Crowd: ‘You Haven’t Heard the Last of Me’ 

In between, a mixture of rising stars and bona fide legends showed up to either introduce or pay musical tribute to the Class of 2026 — or, in some cases, the inductees themselves got in on the action. The full Wu-Tang Clan hit the stage for a medley, while Queen Latifah and MC Lyte joined forces for a joint performance celebrating their contributions as women in hip-hop, Billy Idol and his longtime guitarist Steve Stevens did one solo song and one duet with a famous face, and Peter Hook of Joy Division and New Order was surrounded by superfans for a celebration of his dual groups.

The through-line of the night was innovation. While the Rock Hall has expanded far beyond the genre of rock & roll, each member of the new class has something vital in common: They changed music for generations to come.

items.title: Tout selling £1million of U2 tickets has raised questions about clampdown on bot use for bulk-buying
items.summary:
A ticket tout has advertised more than £1million worth of tickets for U2 ‘s upcoming London shows, raising fresh questions about the use of automated bots to bulk-buy tickets and sell them on at inflated prices.

READ MORE: As live music returns, let’s build back fairer – by wiping out unscrupulous touts 

The Irish band’s four nights at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in June 2027, part of their ‘The Greatest Show On Earth’ world tour , sold out shortly after tickets went on sale last week.

However, a new investigation by The Guardian has revealed that one seller listed more than 2,000 tickets for the concerts on resale site StubHub, despite strict limits on the number that any individual buyer can purchase.

The seller, identified as Vladyslav Skrypka and claiming to be based in Harlow, Essex, advertised over 1,800 tickets for one night alone, some at more than four times their original price. If all of the tickets were sold at their advertised prices, they would generate more than £1million in sales.

The findings have raised concerns about how such large quantities of tickets can be obtained, given that the use of automated software to bypass ticket-buying limits has been outlawed in the UK since 2018 .

Adam Webb of the music industry campaign group FanFair Alliance suggested that the listings could indicate either the use of bots or ‘speculative selling’ – where touts advertise tickets they do not yet possess, hoping to acquire them after a buyer has paid.

View this post on Instagram

The long-awaited spin-off of Eurovision held its inaugural final at the One Bangkok Forum in Thailand yesterday (November 14), with 11 countries competing for the title.

Carmelle, whose full name is Carmelle Collado, finished with 211 points, receiving 93 from the national juries and 118 from the public vote. She topped both categories to finish 41 points ahead of the host country’s representatives, MANG x DAOU, whose song ‘Aroma’ received 170 points.

Vietnam’s Tóc Tiên finished third with ‘EM TIÊN’ on 164 points, while Malaysia and Laos completed the top five.

Carmelle’s winning song ‘Sobra-Sobra’, meaning ‘Too Much’, is a women’s empowerment anthem that combines dance-pop and rap with traditional Filipino instruments, including the kubing and kulintang.

Watch the winning performance below:

Speaking after her victory, Carmelle described the song as “a tribute to all Filipino women”.

“I made history, since this was the first time,” she told the Associated Press. “It’s such a big responsibility for me, because this one is a global stage, so thank you everybody who voted for me.”

The singer, who grew up in the Bicol region of the Philippines, previously found success on televised singing competitions, finishing as runner-up on The Voice Kids and winning Tawag ng Tanghalan . She also appeared on Pinoy Big Brother .

items.title: Daniel Hall, Co-Founder of Australian Rock Band Taxiride, Dies at 48
items.summary:
Daniel Hall, a co-founder of the Australian rock band Taxiride, died Friday (Nov. 13). He was 48.

The band announced his death in a social media post. “It is with the heaviest of hearts we announce the passing of our youngest brother in arms, Daniel James Hall,” it read. “We shared some amazing experiences and his departure doesn’t seem real. Rest In Peace Dan.”

In a separate post on Hall’s own page, his partner, Jess, said he died unexpectedly at home in the early hours of Friday. “I am completely devastated,” she wrote. “Your prayers and kind messages are appreciated.” No cause has been given.

Taxiride formed in Melbourne in the late ’90s, after Tim Watson and Tim Wild began writing together and were joined by Jason Singh and Hall, who had spent years busking in the suburb of Camberwell and playing Melbourne venues. The four-piece signed to Warner after recording a demo at the city’s Secret Sound Studios.

Their 1999 debut, Imaginate , produced by Jack Joseph Puig and recorded between Ocean Way in Los Angeles and Secret Sound, went to No. 1 on the ARIA albums chart and was certified double platinum in Australia. It was released in the U.S. on Warner/Sire.

Lead single “Get Set” reached No. 8 on the ARIA singles chart and No. 36 on Billboard’s Modern Rock Tracks chart, and won breakthrough artist – single at the 1999 ARIA Awards. It was also nominated for best pop release. Follow-up “Everywhere You Go” gave the band a second ARIA top 15 hit, and Imaginate drew two further ARIA nominations the following year.

Hall left Taxiride in 2001 to pursue solo work and later…
items.t: Daniel Hall, Co-Founder of Australian Rock Band Taxiride, Dies at 48

items.title: U2 Opens 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Ceremony With Surprise Performance
items.summary:
U2 crashed the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony on Saturday night (Nov. 14), opening the show at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater with a surprise two-song set a day after releasing their new album, Carnaval De Luz .

The band weren’t on the bill — they were inducted back in 2005, their first year of eligibility — but they kicked off the night for a class that included Phil Collins , Billy Idol, Iron Maiden, Joy Division/New Order, Oasis, Sade, Luther Vandross and Wu-Tang Clan.

They opened with “Silencio,” the album’s second single, joined by a line of performers dressed as riot police and carrying shields, then closed with “Pride (In the Name of Love),” a fixture of their live shows for four decades.

Carnaval De Luz , out Friday (Nov. 13) via Interscope, is U2’s 16th album and their first full-length of new material since 2017’s Songs of Experience . It was produced by longtime collaborator Jacknife Lee, and its title translates as “Carnival of Light.” The cover, showing the band walking single file along a beach with Bono out front in a top hat, is a clear nod to Abbey Road .

The album closes with “Torn,” a duet with Dolly Parton that her representative has confirmed is her final recorded vocal performance. Parton died in August at 80. U2 wrote the song with Parton and Snow Patrol’s Johnny McDaid, and have described it as a country song about broken family ties.

The release also gives U2 a shot at extending a Billboard 200 record. Songs of Experience was their eighth No. 1, making them the only group to top the chart in four consecutive decades. They’ve…

items.title: Phil Collins Tells Rock Hall Crowd: ‘You Haven’t Heard the Last of Me’
items.summary:
Phil Collins was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame as a solo artist on Saturday (Nov. 14), and used his acceptance speech to tell the crowd he isn’t done yet.

“You haven’t heard the last of me,” Collins said during the ceremony at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. “I promise you that.”

The honor marks Collins’ second induction. He entered the Hall in 2010 as a member of Genesis , making him one of a small number of two-time inductees.

Travis Barker inducted Collins, highlighting his impact as a drummer. “I remember hearing the drums for the first time and being blown away,” the Blink-182 drummer said of “In the Air Tonight.” “That sound changed everything. It helped define the sound of drums in the eighties, and you can still hear Phil’s influence today.”

Barker also pointed to Collins’ success with both Genesis and his solo career. “He wasn’t just successful at both,” he said, “he was one of the best at both.”

Collins did not perform at the ceremony. He said earlier this year that he had declined an invitation to play because he wasn’t “match-fit” enough to rehearse and sing properly, though he did not rule out returning to the stage. Cynthia Erivo performed “In the Air Tonight” in his place, with Barker on drums.

In his speech, Collins said he felt unprepared following a night of more polished addresses, and opened by telling the audience he’s “really not as bad as it looks.” He said his career began with a single goal: “I grew up wanting to play drums. Everything else has been a happy accident.”

Collins credited his assistant with saving his life,…
items.t: Phil Collins Tells Rock Hall Crowd: ‘You Haven’t Heard the Last of Me’

items.title: BTS & ROSÉ Lead a Big Night for K-Pop at 2026 Kids’ Choice Awards: Full Winners List
items.summary:
Kids love K-Pop. That was abundantly clear from the results at the 2026 Kids’ Choice Awards, which aired on CBS for the first time on Saturday (Nov. 14). BTS won three major awards, though they weren’t at Television City in Hollywood for the taping, nor did they accept any of their awards by video, as ROSÉ and “global girl group” KATSEYE did.

BTS won favorite group for a record-extending fifth time; favorite song (“Swim”) for a second time and favorite album ( ARIRANG ) for the first time. In the favorite song category, BTS had won five years ago for “Dynamite.” The only other group or duo to win twice in the category is One Direction (back-to-back awards in 2013-14 for “What Makes You Beautiful” and “Story of My Life”). (The Kids’ Choice Awards originated in 1987.)

Related 

Alex Warren ‘Would Be Shocked’ If 2026 Kids’ Choice Awards Doesn’t Break a Slime Record During His Hosting Debut: ‘It’s a Priority of Mine’

items.title: James Blunt: ‘Do I have a nickname? Yes, it rhymes with blunt’
items.summary:
The singer on his love for Ibiza, the weirdest thing he’s done in the name of romance, and being signed up for Celebrity Traitors against his will

You were a punching bag for such a long time after You’re Beautiful became a massive hit but your consistent good humour is deeply admirable. Does it ever get tiring?

It was a surprise, at the beginning. I was just a little guy with a dream. And when you achieve your dream, you think people would be happy for you. For them not to be happy for you but angry with you, for your song, seems irrational, an overreaction. It is interesting how people generally want to tear people down for achieving their little dreams. But I’d had a real proper job before that [as a captain in the British army]. My friends might have been on operations in Afghanistan or Iraq, so if I were to complain to them at the time saying, “Oh, the Guardian said something really horrid about me and gave me three stars for my album” – they would be able to talk about who had lost their lives or limbs that day, and that put it all in perspective. And perspective is everything.

items.title: Sheherazaad: Khudgarzi review | Ammar Kalia's global album of the month
items.summary:
(Erased Tapes)
Dreamy, reverb-laden arrangements, virtuosic vocals and echoes of PJ Harvey and Massive Attack make this disarming debut a one-of-a-kind creation

Since the release of her debut EP, Qasr, in 2024, south Asian-American vocalist and composer Sheherazaad has developed a distinctive take on the classical singing of her heritage. While her contemporaries such as the singers Ganavya and Manizeh draw on spiritual vocal traditions, and Arooj Aftab on jazz and folk instrumentation, Sheherazaad’s work is darker and far more introspective, using sparse acoustic arrangements to create a style of Urdu-language noir.

On this debut album, she delivers her most disarmingly eerie and mournful work yet. A heavy layer of reverb coats the record’s spare and often evocative arrangements, making undulating tabla hits echo beneath Sheherazaad’s keening vocals on Qatil, while on Registaan it lends an unnervingly distorted quality to a simple guitar refrain and on Mard it subsumes melody in a haze of resonance. The resulting atmosphere sits somewhere between PJ Harvey’s late-90s eerie grunge and the trip-hop qawwali of Massive Attack’s work with singer Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan – an ambience that is…

items.title: Hamlet Hail to the Thief could have been rotten but redeems Radiohead’s ‘record that got away’ | Alexis Petridis
items.summary:
The band’s uneven 2003 album has been judiciously reworked to accompany a staging of Shakespeare’s tragedy with quite extraordinary results

According to the programme notes, Thom Yorke had serious reservations about director Christine Jones’ idea to stage a production of Hamlet featuring music from Radiohead’s 2003 album Hail to the Thief. Who can blame him? Many criticisms have been laid at Radiohead’s door but being hopelessly naff isn’t one of them, and, alas, naff is very much the adjective you’d apply to a lot of attempts to meld Shakespeare and rock music.

You’re often in the realm of high camp – portentous, Bard-quoting heavy metal lyrics; Return to the Forbidden Planet’s jokey blending of The Tempest with 50s rock’n’roll; 2015’s These Paper Bullets, which relocated Much Ado About Nothing to swinging London, complete with Beatle-y songs by Green Day’s Billie Joe Armstrong – or of buttock-clenching disasters like Catch My Soul, a 1971 rock adaptation of Othello which required Black American soul singer PP Arnold to star opposite impresario Jack Good, playing the title role in blackface.

items.title: ‘Joni Mitchell sang Both Sides, Now over the phone to me’: folk music legend Judy Collins on her 87 remarkable years
items.summary:
As she continues her farewell tour, the US singer-songwriter answers your questions on romance with Stephen Stills, friendship with Carly Simon and how folk underpins all pop

How did you come into Joni Mitchell’s orbit and how did you end up recording Both Sides, Now before she did? Steve-bayley
I’m 48 years sober, but in the old days I drank. One night in 1967, I was passed out and the phone rang at about 3am. It was my friend [the musician, songwriter and producer] Al Kooper. He said he’d been at a club and had run into this woman, Joni, who wrote songs. He put her on the phone and she sang Both Sides, Now over the phone. It was brilliant. I said: “I’ll be right over.” I recorded it the next day and it became a huge hit.

I don’t think Joni was too happy that I was the first to record it, but she was very generous and I’ve since recorded many of her songs. She was unknown then, so I’m proud that I was able to help introduce her to the world. She’s one of the great writers of all time.

items.title: Blackhaine: Saints in the Wethouse review | Alexis Petridis's album of the week
items.summary:
(XL Recordings)
His Playboi Carti collabs may have dragged Tom Heyes out of the underground, but this bracing debut remains far from the mainstream, full of garbled barks and walls of noise

On the second track on his debut album, Tom Heyes accuses lesser artists of copying him. “What the fuck you even take me for?” he barks on Northside Needs Me, over a grinding, distorted bassline that comes punctuated with stammering, rave-y vocal samples. “Too much noise shit, replicating what I played before.”

Of course, charging that others are merely imitating what you did previously is a venerable rap tradition: the track that gave said practice its longstanding name, Bite’n My Stylee by Original Concept, is now 40 years old. Perhaps it’s true that others have been copying the approach that Heyes has minted under the alias of Blackhaine, but if so, it seems faintly remarkable, because his approach is so determinedly unique.

items.title: ‘Young, Black and female in Brixton is hard’: ​from football to Top Boy and wordplay, the inspiring journey of UK rapper Cristale
items.summary:
Crystal Palace FC or Oxbridge beckoned, but the multitalented MC kept forging her way towards music. She explains how she poured every aspect of herself into her debut mixtape

Two weeks before we meet, UK rapper Cristale was scrambling down a cliff face to a secluded black pebbled beach in Dover, racing an incoming tide with fewer than 90 minutes to shoot the video for her single I’m Okay With Being Lonely. She’d never hiked before in her life. “I was wearing head-to-toe Stone Island, no hiking gear, full face of makeup, edges laid and Mum was doing my touch-ups on a rusty ladder,” she laughs.

As we sit in her publicist’s central London office, her hair half-braided and half-flowing past a black puffer coat, she says the rush of adrenaline hasn’t fully faded. In fact she seems to thrive on regular bumps of it: beyond her relentlessly articulate and energetic rap flow – put to work on tracks that span drill, introspective R&B and beyond – she has ably hopped between football, art, acting in Netflix projects and more.

items.title: ‘My partners would all tell you I was a nut job’: Jane Wiedlin on the Go-Go’s, fame and the freedom of sex dungeons
items.summary:
As she releases a brutally honest memoir, the new wave icon opens up about industry sexism, living with bipolar disorder and becoming ‘the world’s first atheist ordained minister’

The first thing Jane Wiedlin tells me before our interview even begins is that, an hour or so earlier, she downed two beers. “It keeps me cheerful,” she says with a laugh. The disclosure dovetails with the reason we’re doing the interview in the first place, which is to unpack her new memoir, a tome that deserves a truth-in-advertising award for its title alone: TMI (as in “too much information”). “I’ve always been TMI!” Wiedlin proudly announces. “I’m the one who always wanted to expose the truth. This book is my first opportunity to do so.”

A portion of that truth has to do with the band she helped form in the late 70s, the Go-Go’s. The five-piece are not only the first all-female band who play their own instruments and write their own material to earn a No 1 album in the US but, astonishingly, are the only such group to hold that distinction nearly 45 years later. The group’s power-pop music, heard in zippy hits like Our Lips Are Sealed and Vacation, led to their induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2021, inspired a Broadway play and influenced modern female artists all the way from Olivia Rodrigo to Wet Leg.

items.t: ‘My partners would all tell you I was a nut job’: Jane Wiedlin on the Go-Go’s, fame and the freedom of sex dungeons
